advertising.sample:
I would like to talk about an unforgettable public service commercial about road safety that I encountered a couple of years ago on YouTube. It was launched by a transport authority to deter reckless speeding.

The advert depicted a split-second right before a horrific head-on collision between two vehicles. Miraculously, time froze, allowing both motorists to step out and talk. One driver remorsefully admitted he had misjudged the intersection, while the other pleaded that his young boy was in the back seat and there was no time to brake. After realizing the collision was unavoidable, they silently stepped back inside, and time resumed with a devastating impact.

What made this commercial exceptionally memorable was its emotional gravity and masterful storytelling. Instead of relying on gratuitous gore or cheap shock tactics, it focused purely on human vulnerability and regret. It powerfully conveyed that a momentary lapse in concentration can irreversibly destroy innocent lives. That haunting scene genuinely changed my driving habits, constantly reminding me to remain vigilant whenever I take the wheel.

p1.q: Do you often see advertisements when you browse the internet?
p1.a: Constantly, to be honest. Whenever I scroll through Instagram feeds or read digital newspapers, targeted banners and sponsored posts appear everywhere. For instance, right after researching wireless headphones, related ads instantly flooded my screen.

p1.q: Have you ever bought something directly because of an advert?
p1.a: Yes, on a few occasions. A while back, I purchased an ergonomic desk chair after seeing a persuasive video clip on TikTok explaining its lumbar support benefits. Fortunately, the product actually lived up to its promises.

p1.q: What kind of advertisements do you find most annoying?
p1.a: I thoroughly detest unskippable video ads that abruptly disrupt music streams or instructional videos. They completely break my concentration and, paradoxically, make me develop an aversion toward whatever brand is being aggressively promoted.

p3.q: In what ways has digital advertising transformed consumer behavior in recent years?
p3.a: Digital advertising has fostered a culture of immediate gratification. Through sophisticated algorithms and frictionless one-click purchasing, marketing messages now induce frequent impulse buying rather than calculated shopping. For example, personalized promotions on social media nudge individuals toward acquiring products they never originally intended to possess. Consequently, modern consumption has noticeably transitioned from being strictly necessity-driven to predominantly emotionally charged.

p3.q: Should governments introduce stricter regulations on advertisements aimed at children?
p3.a: Definitely, as young minds lack the critical faculties required to distinguish promotional hyperbole from reality. Unchecked commercials promoting sugary confectionery or violent merchandise frequently distort children's dietary habits and behavioral patterns. While businesses might lament the loss of commercial freedom, safeguarding child well-being must always take precedence over corporate profits. Therefore, enacting strict bans on deceptive promotional tactics targeting minors is thoroughly justified.

mistakesVi: Lặp đi lặp lại danh từ 'advertisement' thay vì sử dụng đa dạng các từ như 'commercial', 'billboard', 'sponsored content', hoặc 'ad campaign'.
Dùng sai kết hợp từ phổ biến, chẳng hạn nói 'make an advertisement' thay vì 'run an ad' hay 'launch an advertising campaign'.

art.sample: I'd like to share an encounter with a mesmerizing piece of art that truly stood out to me. It is an oil painting titled 'Dawn over the Terraces', created by a local contemporary painter named Hoang Vu. I stumbled upon it about two years ago while exploring a cozy art boutique in downtown Hanoi. Visually, the canvas captures the cascading rice terraces of northern Vietnam right at sunrise. It is dominated by a rich palette of golden yellows and lush emerald greens, contrasted by the soft, diffused morning mist drifting between the valleys. What captivated me most was the artist's textured brushwork; you could almost feel the cool morning dew and the gentle breeze sweeping across the fields. The reason this painting left such an indelible mark on me is the overwhelming sense of serenity it conveyed. Living in a bustling, high-stress city, standing before that artwork felt like an emotional retreat. It wasn't merely a technical triumph with intricate detail, but a thought-provoking celebration of rural tranquility that instantly lowered my heart rate and made me appreciate the simple beauty of nature.

p1.q: Do you enjoy visiting art galleries or exhibitions?
p1.a: Honestly, yes. I find wandering through exhibitions quite therapeutic, as it offers a creative escape from daily routines. Just last month, I visited an impressionist gallery, and the dynamic use of light totally fascinated me.

p1.q: Did you learn how to draw or paint when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, we had mandatory art classes in primary school where we sketched basic objects like fruits and landscapes. Although I lacked natural talent, mixing watercolors was always the highlight of my week.

p1.q: Do you have any artwork displayed on the walls of your home?
p1.a: We do have a couple of minimalist canvas prints in our living room. They feature abstract geometric patterns that complement our modern furniture and bring a welcoming, aesthetic vibe to the entire space.

p3.q: Why do some people consider traditional art forms more valuable than digital artwork?
p3.a: I think traditional art is often seen as more authentic because it requires physical mastery of tangible materials, like canvas and clay. Each piece is unique and impossible to replicate identically. In contrast, digital art can be duplicated with a single click, which sometimes diminishes its perceived rarity. Consequently, collectors are willing to pay a premium for physical works that represent irreversible craftsmanship.

p3.q: Should governments allocate significant public funds to support artists and cultural institutions?
p3.a: Without question, government funding is essential for preserving a nation's cultural heritage and fostering creativity. While some argue that public money should prioritize healthcare or infrastructure, art institutions enrich society spiritually and attract tourism. Without state subsidies, independent artists would struggle to survive financially, potentially leading to the decline of traditional cultural expressions that define national identity.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'picture' để chỉ mọi tác phẩm nghệ thuật; nên dùng từ vựng chính xác hơn như 'painting' (tranh vẽ màu), 'sketch' (bản phác thảo), 'portrait' (chân dung) hay 'sculpture' (tác phẩm điêu khắc).

birthdays.sample: I would like to share the story of an exceptionally meaningful birthday present I received on my eighteenth birthday. It was a handcrafted photo scrapbook compiled by my childhood best friend, Linh. Inside, she had meticulously assembled photographs documenting our friendship from primary school right through high school, accompanied by handwritten anecdotes and inside jokes we had shared over the years. When she handed it to me wrapped in rustic brown paper, I had anticipated a standard shop-bought item, so uncovering this labor of love took me completely by surprise. In fact, flipping through the pages made me tear up because it revived so many forgotten memories. What made this keepsake irreplaceable was its immense sentimental value. Turning eighteen felt daunting as we were about to head to different universities, but this album served as a tangible reminder of our enduring bond. In an era where digital messages and mass-produced goods dominate, knowing someone dedicated weeks to crafting something personal just for me was profoundly touching. It remains the most precious birthday gift I have ever received.

p1.q: How do you usually celebrate your birthday?
p1.a: I generally opt for a low-key celebration with my immediate family and closest friends. Typically, we prepare a hearty home-cooked meal and share a cake, as I find intimate gatherings much more meaningful than throwing noisy parties.

p1.q: What kind of gifts do you prefer receiving from your close friends?
p1.a: I definitely appreciate personalized or experiential presents rather than expensive items. For instance, a thoughtful book picked specifically for my reading tastes or concert tickets to a shared favorite band holds far greater significance for me.

p1.q: Do you think it is difficult to choose a suitable present for someone?
p1.a: Yes, it can be quite challenging because balancing someone's distinct preferences with practicality requires effort. Unless you know the recipient deeply, there is always a lingering risk of gifting something redundant that ends up unused in a drawer.

p3.q: In what ways has the way people celebrate birthdays evolved compared to previous generations?
p3.a: In the past, birthday festivities in Vietnam were modest occasions centered strictly around family meals and home cooking. Today, influenced heavily by social media culture and higher disposable income, celebrations have grown noticeably lavish. Young people frequently hire aesthetic venues, curate themed parties, or travel abroad. While this encourages creative expression, it sometimes shifts the focus from authentic bonding toward staging pictures for online validation.

p3.q: Do you believe commercialization has diminished the genuine sentimental value of giving presents?
p3.a: To a certain extent, yes. Aggressive corporate advertising often equates genuine affection with exorbitant price tags, pressuring consumers into buying luxury goods simply to conform to social expectations. Nevertheless, sentimental value has not vanished entirely. Many individuals still prioritize hand-crafted or uniquely personalized tokens of appreciation, demonstrating that genuine emotional intent continues to outweigh pure monetary cost.

mistakesVi: Lặp từ vựng đơn điệu 'gift' và 'present' xuyên suốt bài mà không sử dụng các từ thay thế linh hoạt như 'token of appreciation', 'keepsake', hoặc 'personalized memento'.
Dịch từng từ tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh không tự nhiên, chẳng hạn dùng 'open a party' thay vì các collocation chuẩn như 'throw a party' hoặc 'host a gathering'.
Nhầm lẫn thì động từ khi nói về trải nghiệm nhận quà trong quá khứ, ví dụ dùng hiện tại hoàn thành 'I have received it when I was 15' thay vì quá khứ đơn 'I received it when I was 15'.

Ý 2: Miêu tả việc ông âm thầm lập quỹ hỗ trợ bệnh nhi ung thư và luôn đối xử tử tế với đoàn làm phim.

celebrities.sample:
I would like to talk about Keanu Reeves, a world-renowned Canadian actor whom I truly look up to. He is best known for his stellar roles in blockbuster franchises like The Matrix and John Wick, establishing himself as an undeniable household name across the globe.

Despite his immense fame and fortune, Keanu leads a remarkably modest lifestyle. What impresses me most is how he consistently uses his platform for the greater good. Having experienced severe personal tragedy, he quietly established a private charitable foundation that funds cancer research and children's hospitals, deliberately keeping his name off the organization to avoid media attention. Furthermore, there are countless documented stories of him treating film crews with genuine kindness and taking pay cuts so that crew members could receive fair compensation.

I admire him immensely because he redefines what it means to be a celebrity. In an industry often dominated by vanity and sensational media circuses, he remains remarkably grounded and generous. His humility and empathy serve as a refreshing reminder that true influence comes from how you treat others rather than the glamour of fame.

p1.q: Do you follow any famous people on social media?
p1.a: Yes, I follow a few tech innovators and professional athletes on Instagram. For instance, I follow Cristiano Ronaldo because his daily workout routines and relentless discipline keep me motivated to stay fit.

p1.q: Who was your favorite celebrity when you were a child?
p1.a: When I was younger, I was a massive fan of Jackie Chan. I loved his action-comedy films like Rush Hour because his stunt work was thrilling yet genuinely hilarious to watch.

p1.q: Would you like to be famous in the future?
p1.a: Not really, because I deeply value my personal privacy. Being constantly scrutinized in the public eye seems overwhelming, and I would much rather achieve quiet professional success without unwanted media attention.

p3.q: Do you think celebrities have a moral responsibility to be positive role models for young people?
p3.a: I believe they do, to a certain extent. Because celebrities possess massive cultural influence, impressionable teenagers often emulate their behavior, fashion, and values. For instance, when a pop star promotes mental health awareness, it can destigmatize seeking therapy for thousands. However, we should not expect them to be flawless saints, as they are ultimately ordinary human beings under intense pressure.

p3.q: How has social media changed the relationship between public figures and their fans?
p3.a: Social media has fundamentally bridged the gap between stars and their audience. In the past, famous people were distant and mysterious, accessible only through television or magazines. Nowadays, platforms like TikTok and Instagram allow celebrities to share unedited moments of their daily lives, creating a sense of intimacy. However, this hyper-accessibility can also fuel unhealthy parasocial relationships and toxic online harassment.

childhood.sample: I'd like to talk about kite flying, an outdoor pastime that defined my childhood summers. Back in the early 2000s, my family lived near an expansive meadow on the outskirts of our town. Every breezy late afternoon, a bunch of neighborhood kids and I would dash out there after finishing our homework. We actually fashioned our own kites out of bamboo strips, old newspapers, and cooked rice paste, which made the experience even more rewarding. We would sprint against the wind, tugging the strings frantically until the kites soared high into the twilight sky. It was utterly thrilling to watch our homemade creations glide above the open fields. This activity left an indelible mark on me because it was completely free from digital distractions. It taught me patience and manual dexterity, as making the kite balance properly was no easy feat. More importantly, those carefree afternoons forged unbreakable bonds between us, and whenever I spot a kite fluttering today, it instantly transports me back to those halcyon days of pure innocence.

p1.q: Did you enjoy your childhood?
p1.a: Definitely, yes. I had an exceptionally joyful upbringing surrounded by loving relatives and lively neighborhood peers. We spent most afternoons playing outdoors until sunset, which gave me countless sweet memories that I still cherish today.

p1.q: What was your favourite game to play when you were younger?
p1.a: I was head over heels for hide-and-seek. My friends and I would scout out every nook and cranny in our apartment complex, and the sheer thrill of evading detection made it an irresistible daily ritual.

p1.q: Who was your closest friend during your primary school years?
p1.a: That would be Minh, my next-door neighbor. We sat at the same desk in class and shared virtually everything, from comic books to secret snacks, forming a genuine bond that lasted all the way through high school.

p3.q: How have children's leisure activities changed compared to several decades ago?
p3.a: In the past, children's pastimes were largely outdoors and community-oriented, revolving around spontaneous physical games like tag or skipping rope. In contrast, modern youngsters gravitate toward solitary screen time, such as playing video games or streaming videos on tablets. While this shift certainly enhances tech literacy from an early age, it unfortunately deprives kids of valuable physical exercise and organic social interaction with their peers.

p3.q: To what extent does a person's childhood environment shape their adult personality?
p3.a: I firmly believe childhood circumstances lay the groundwork for adulthood. Growing up in a secure, supportive household typically fosters emotional stability and self-confidence, whereas enduring prolonged adversity or neglect might lead to chronic anxiety later in life. Of course, adult experiences and conscious self-development can reshape one's outlook, but the behavioral patterns established during one's formative years undeniably remain the bedrock of adult identity.

city.sample: A bustling location in my city that I know like the back of my hand is Nguyen Hue Pedestrian Street, situated right in the heart of District 1, Ho Chi Minh City. This vibrant promenade attracts an eclectic mix of people. On any given evening, you’ll see local teenagers hanging out, buskers showcasing their talents, and foreign tourists soaking up the nightlife. Families with young children also flock there to take leisurely strolls. People engage in a variety of activities here. Youngsters often gather to skate or record dance videos, while others pop into the trendy cafes housed in the famous vintage apartment building nearby. Food vendors dot the perimeter, offering popular street snacks like grilled rice paper. Personally, I have a love-hate relationship with this place. On the one hand, I’m drawn to its infectious energy, which makes it an ideal spot to unwind after a gruelling week. On the other hand, it gets packed to the rafters on weekends, and the sheer volume of noise can sometimes be overwhelming. Nevertheless, it remains the beating heart of the city.

p1.q: Do you live in a city or in the countryside?
p1.a: I currently live in a bustling city, specifically Hanoi. I really appreciate the convenience here because modern amenities like shopping malls and hospitals are virtually on my doorstep, even though the air quality can occasionally be a downside.

p1.q: What is your favourite place in your city?
p1.a: My go-to spot is definitely West Lake. It offers a peaceful escape from downtown noise, and I love cycling around the water at sunset while grabbing an iced coffee with friends to unwind.

p1.q: Is it easy to get around where you live?
p1.a: Generally, yes, because ride-hailing apps and bus routes are readily accessible and affordable. However, during rush hour, navigating the streets becomes a nightmare due to bumper-to-bumper traffic jams along major intersections.

p3.q: Will more people move to cities in the future?
p3.a: I believe urbanisation will definitely accelerate in the coming decades. Cities offer superior employment prospects, state-of-the-art healthcare, and premier educational institutions that rural areas simply lack. While living costs and housing shortages in metropolitan areas are rising steeply, the promise of higher living standards and career growth will continue to lure young professionals away from the countryside.

p3.q: How can cities reduce traffic jams?
p3.a: Governments should primarily invest heavily in comprehensive public transit networks, such as underground metro lines and electric buses, to make collective transport more enticing than private vehicles. Additionally, implementing congestion charges for cars entering central districts during peak hours could discourage unnecessary driving. Combining reliable infrastructure with financial disincentives is crucial to unclogging urban roads.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'busy' hoặc 'crowded': Người học hay lặp lại các từ đơn giản này; nên thay bằng 'packed to the rafters', 'bustling', hoặc 'swarming with people'.
Dịch 'kẹt xe' theo kiểu tiếng Việt: Dùng sai thành 'have traffic jam' hoặc 'traffic is stuck'; cách diễn đạt chuẩn là 'get stuck in traffic' hoặc 'experience gridlock'.

clothes.sample: I would like to talk about a tailor-made navy blue suit that I reserve exclusively for milestone celebrations. I received it as a university graduation gift from my parents two years ago, handcrafted by a reputable tailor in downtown Hanoi. Aesthetically, it boasts a sleek, modern cut crafted from breathable wool-blend fabric, featuring subtle satin lapels that add a touch of understated elegance. Unlike mass-produced off-the-rack garments, this suit fits like a glove and feels remarkably comfortable throughout long events. I generally slip into this suit on high-profile occasions, such as formal family weddings, high-stakes job interviews, and annual Tet banquets. Because it requires delicate dry cleaning, I only wear it perhaps three or four times each year. There are two primary reasons why I truly cherish this outfit. First, putting it on gives me an instant boost of confidence, helping me present myself with poise and maturity. More importantly, it holds immense sentimental value, constantly reminding me of my family's unwavering encouragement as I stepped out into the professional world.

p1.q: What kinds of clothes do you usually like to wear?
p1.a: I tend to gravitate towards casual and minimalist attire. On a typical day, I usually opt for breathable cotton T-shirts paired with relaxed-fit chinos, mainly because comfort is my top priority when commuting or working.

p1.q: Do you prefer shopping for clothes online or in physical stores?
p1.a: I definitely prefer brick-and-mortar shops. Being able to try garments on and feel the fabric firsthand prevents sizing blunders, like when I once bought an oversized jumper online that looked completely unflattering in real life.

p1.q: Did you have to wear a school uniform when you were younger?
p1.a: Yes, throughout my secondary school years, we were mandated to wear white button-downs and navy trousers. Although it felt somewhat rigid back then, it genuinely eliminated peer pressure regarding trendy branded clothes.

p3.q: Why do some people spend an excessive amount of money on designer brands?
p3.a: In my view, many individuals splurge on luxury fashion primarily to project social status and success. Wearing recognizable designer logos acts as a badge of prestige, boosting their self-esteem in social circles. While a minority might genuinely appreciate exceptional craftsmanship, the majority are driven by peer validation and materialism. Consequently, aggressive brand marketing capitalizes heavily on this desire to display wealth.

p3.q: How has the rise of fast fashion impacted the environment and consumer behavior?
p3.a: Fast fashion has drastically accelerated textile waste and environmental pollution through cheap, synthetic fabrics. Furthermore, it has cultivated an unhealthy throwaway culture among consumers, where garments are discarded after just a few wears rather than repaired. Although low prices democratize trendy clothing, the ecological consequences—ranging from microplastics to water contamination—are simply unsustainable. Therefore, embracing sustainable, circular fashion has become critical.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai ngữ pháp từ 'clothes': Từ này luôn ở dạng số nhiều và không có 'a clothe'. Để chỉ một chiếc áo/quần, phải dùng 'an item of clothing', 'a piece of clothing' hoặc 'a garment'.

environment.sample: In my neighbourhood in Hanoi, plastic waste has become a pressing issue. Everywhere you look, especially around traditional wet markets, discarded plastic bags and single-use containers are piling up, clogging drainage systems and spoiling the local landscape. To tackle this, I believe promoting reusable tote bags and food containers is the most practical solution. Shoppers could simply bring their own canvas bags and multi-use boxes instead of grabbing handfuls of flimsy plastic bags from vendors. At the same time, shopkeepers should charge a small nominal fee for every plastic bag provided, which immediately discourages careless usage. Regarding responsibility, it has to be a joint effort. Local authorities need to run awareness campaigns and enforce bag fees, but ultimately, residents themselves must change their mindset and break away from this throwaway culture. I'm confident this approach would work wonders. Supermarkets in my city have already started charging for carrier bags, and people adapted remarkably quickly. If local markets do the same, we could cut neighbourhood waste by half within a year.

p1.q: Is the environment important to you?
p1.a: Absolutely, it's vital to me because our well-being directly depends on it. Breathing polluted air or drinking contaminated water ruins our health, so I believe keeping our surroundings clean ensures a much higher quality of life for everyone.

p1.q: What do you do to protect the environment?
p1.a: I try to minimize my carbon footprint by commuting via public transit or cycling instead of riding a motorbike. Additionally, I always carry a refillable water bottle and avoid single-use plastics whenever I go grocery shopping.

p1.q: Is there an environmental problem where you live?
p1.a: Yes, urban air pollution is a major headache in my city. Heavy traffic congestion and endless construction projects generate thick dust and toxic exhaust fumes, which often trigger respiratory issues for local residents like myself.

p3.q: Should governments or individuals take more responsibility for the environment?
p3.a: I believe both play crucial roles, but governments should lead the way. Authorities have the legislative power to enforce strict emissions standards and invest in renewable energy infrastructure, which individuals simply cannot do alone. That being said, top-down policies will only bear fruit if citizens actively sort their waste and adopt greener lifestyles. In essence, state regulations provide the framework, while individual actions drive genuine change.

p3.q: How can schools teach children to care for the environment?
p3.a: Schools can make environmental education hands-on rather than purely theoretical. For instance, teachers can organize regular campus clean-ups or guide pupils in maintaining a school vegetable garden and composting food scraps. When youngsters witness the direct impact of conservation firsthand, it resonates far deeper than textbook lectures. This practical exposure helps instill lifelong sustainable habits from an early age.

p3.q: Do families spend enough time together nowadays?
p3.a: In my view, many families struggle to spend meaningful quality time together nowadays. With demanding work schedules and the ubiquitous presence of digital devices, family members often sit in the same room while remaining glued to their smartphones. For instance, shared conversations are frequently displaced by social media scrolling. Consequently, emotional intimacy can gradually weaken unless households make a deliberate effort to disconnect from screens and engage with one another.

p3.q: How have family structures changed in your country?
p3.a: In Vietnam, there has been a marked transition from traditional multi-generational households to nuclear families. Decades ago, it was customary for three generations to reside under the same roof. However, rapid urbanization and an increasing desire for privacy have prompted young couples to purchase their own flats in urban centers. While this fosters greater personal autonomy, it sometimes diminishes the immediate daily support system that extended families historically provided.

I would like to share my experience at the Mid-Autumn Lantern Festival in Hoi An, which I attended two years ago. I traveled there with two of my closest university friends right in the middle of the lunar eighth month, when the ancient town switched off all fluorescent streetlights.

The entire riverside was illuminated by thousands of colorful, handcrafted silk lanterns. We spent the evening weaving through bustling alleyways, watching energetic lion dances, and sampling traditional baked mooncakes sold by street vendors. Later on, we hired a wooden boat to gently drift down the Thu Bon River and released glowing paper lanterns into the water while making personal wishes.

What made this experience unforgettable was the enchanting ambience and the profound sense of harmony. In our fast-paced modern routines, we rarely pause to appreciate intangible cultural heritage. Being immersed in that warm, golden glow alongside locals and travelers gave me a deep feeling of tranquility and renewed my appreciation for longstanding Vietnamese customs.

p1.q: What is your favorite traditional festival in your country?
p1.a: Without a doubt, Tet or the Lunar New Year is my absolute favorite. It is an invaluable occasion when all family members gather around a warm dinner table, exchange heartfelt wishes, and enjoy customary dishes like Chung cake.

p1.q: How do people usually celebrate public holidays where you live?
p1.a: Most urban residents take advantage of these breaks to travel or meet up with friends. For instance, during National Day, people often flock to pedestrian zones to watch outdoor music concerts and magnificent fireworks.

p1.q: Do you prefer spending festival times with your family or friends?
p1.a: I generally gravitate towards family gatherings for traditional events because they carry nostalgic rituals. However, for modern festivities like New Year's Eve, I prefer counting down with close friends at vibrant street parties.

p3.q: In what ways do commercial promotions alter the traditional essence of cultural festivals?
p3.a: Mass marketing often shifts the focus from spiritual introspection or familial bonding toward relentless consumerism. When holidays become dominated by shopping sprees, festive sales, and superficial packaging, their historical narratives get eclipsed. For instance, Mid-Autumn Festival in urban areas has evolved from an intimate folk reunion into a cutthroat corporate gifting competition, diluting the original values of togetherness and gratitude.

p3.q: Why might younger generations feel less connected to ancient customs and folk celebrations?
p3.a: A major reason is the pervasive influence of globalization and digital entertainment, which presents youth with endless modern distractions. Furthermore, many ancestral ceremonies involve archaic and repetitive formalities that young adults struggle to identify with. Unless these traditions are actively revitalized and contextualized in engaging, modern formats—such as interactive cultural festivals—the generational divide will inevitably widen, leaving young people detached from their cultural roots.

I would like to talk about Phở bò, which is undoubtedly the most iconic traditional dish from Vietnam.

At its core, this dish consists of delicate, flat rice noodles served in a piping-hot, aromatic broth and topped with tender cuts of beef, along with fresh scallions and coriander. The true magic lies in the broth, which is patiently simmered for hours using beef marrow bones, charred ginger, star anise, and cinnamon to achieve an extraordinarily rich, savory depth of flavor.

Traditionally, Vietnamese people savor a bowl of Pho for breakfast to kick-start their day, but nowadays it is enjoyed around the clock, from quick lunches to late-night suppers. It is particularly satisfying on chilly mornings or rainy evenings when that steaming soup warms you from the inside out.

The main reason I adore Pho is its remarkable balance of flavors and textures. It feels nourishing and light rather than greasy, and every single spoonful offers a wonderful sense of nostalgia, reminding me of cozy weekend breakfasts with my grandparents. It is truly the ultimate comfort food.

p1.q: What kind of food do you enjoy most?
p1.a: I am particularly fond of home-cooked Vietnamese meals. I appreciate dishes featuring balanced flavors and plenty of fresh greens, such as sweet and sour fish soup, because they are wholesome and never feel heavy or greasy.

p1.q: Do you enjoy cooking?
p1.a: Yes, absolutely. Preparing meals is a therapeutic way for me to unwind after a stressful day. I genuinely love experimenting with fresh herbs and spices, and whipping up a delicious dinner gives me a great sense of satisfaction.

p1.q: Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants?
p1.a: I generally prefer eating at home because it is far healthier and budget-friendly. However, on weekends, I do occasionally eat out with friends to try diverse international cuisines, like Japanese sushi or authentic Italian pasta.

p3.q: Is fast food a problem in your country?
p3.a: Yes, it is increasingly becoming a serious public health concern, especially among young people in metropolitan areas. Due to hectic work routines, many individuals regularly consume burgers, fried chicken, and sugary drinks. This regular reliance on processed meals has contributed significantly to alarming spikes in childhood obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular complications across modern cities.

p3.q: How has the way people eat changed over the last few decades?
p3.a: In the past, families almost exclusively gathered for home-cooked meals prepared with fresh ingredients bought daily from wet markets. In contrast, modern dining revolves heavily around speed and convenience. The widespread popularity of food delivery apps and ready-to-eat convenience store meals means people often eat on the go, which unfortunately undermines communal family dining traditions and nutritional balance.

Nhầm lẫn giữa danh từ không đếm được 'food' (nói chung) và danh từ đếm được 'foods' (các nhóm hoặc loại thực phẩm cụ thể, như 'processed foods').

I would like to talk about Minh, my closest friend from university. We first met during our freshman orientation week and hit it off almost immediately thanks to our shared love for badminton.

A couple of years ago, I went through a very rough patch when I failed a crucial semester exam while juggling a stressful part-time job. I was on the verge of burning out and seriously contemplated dropping out. Minh noticed I was unusually withdrawn and stepped in without hesitation. Not only did he lend a sympathetic ear when I vented my frustrations, but he also created a structured study plan for me. Every evening for three straight weeks, he patiently walked me through complex accounting concepts and tested my revision.

His generous support bailed me out of academic probation, but more importantly, it restored my shattered self-confidence. I felt deeply indebted and profoundly grateful for his unwavering patience. Knowing that someone believed in me when I doubted myself meant the world. That experience cemented our bond, proving to me that true friends truly stick together through thick and thin.

p1.q: Do you have a close friend?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. My childhood friend Nam has been my confidant for over a decade. We share almost everything from daily trivial gossip to major career plans, and he always supports me whenever I face dilemmas.

p1.q: How often do you meet your friends?
p1.a: I try to catch up with them at least once or twice a week. We usually hang out at a local café on weekends to unwind, chat about our work, and blow off some steam together.

p1.q: Do you prefer meeting friends in person or online?
p1.a: I certainly prefer meeting in person because physical presence allows for genuine emotional connection. You can read body language and share laughs over a meal, whereas texting or video calls often feel somewhat detached.

p3.q: Is it harder to make close friends as an adult?
p3.a: I firmly believe it is. When we are young, shared environments like school create effortless opportunities to bond. As adults, however, people are constrained by heavy workloads and family duties, leaving little spare time. Furthermore, adults naturally become more guarded and cautious about opening up emotionally compared to carefree children. Therefore, cultivating deep, authentic bonds in adulthood demands substantially more intentional effort.

p3.q: Can online friendships be as strong as real-life ones?
p3.a: In my view, while online friendships can be remarkably supportive, they rarely match the depth of real-world relationships. Virtual communication allows people to connect over niche interests regardless of distance, which is wonderful. However, without experiencing shared physical realities and weathering real-life crises side by side, it is harder to build rock-solid trust. Thus, face-to-face interactions still provide a stronger foundation for lifelong camaraderie.

health.sample: I'd like to talk about a habit I've been cultivating over the past year, which is drinking at least two liters of water every single day. I picked up this habit early last year when I started feeling constantly fatigued and suffering from frequent headaches. My doctor pointed out that mild dehydration was the culprit and advised me to increase my daily fluid intake. To keep this up consistently, I bought a large reusable water bottle with time markings on the side, which reminds me when to sip. I also installed a hydration tracker app on my phone that buzzes every hour. In the beginning, it felt tedious to constantly refill my bottle, but after a few weeks, it became second nature. This simple change has truly worked wonders for my health. Not only has my skin cleared up significantly, but my afternoon brain fog has also vanished. I feel far more energized throughout the day and rarely experience tension headaches anymore. Sticking to this routine has really shown me how small daily changes yield huge health rewards.

p1.q: How do you keep healthy?

Affordable medical services ensure that vulnerable populations receive essential treatments without falling into severe medical debt. Therefore, investing in robust healthcare systems benefits society as a whole.

p3.q: Why do many people find it hard to build healthy habits?
p3.a: I think modern lifestyles are the primary culprit. People often juggle demanding work hours and family responsibilities, which leaves them physically drained and prone to choosing quick comfort, like junk food, over exercising. Without strong discipline, it is remarkably easy to fall back into unhealthy routines.

hobbies.sample:
About six months ago, I decided to take up pottery making, which has surprisingly become my favorite pastime. I first stumbled upon it while watching an artisanal craft documentary on YouTube, and seeing the potter transform wet clay into elegant ceramics completely captivated me. I signed up for a beginner workshop at a local studio the very next weekend.

Nowadays, I carve out three hours every Saturday morning to attend studio sessions. During these classes, I practice wheel throwing and hand-building techniques, crafting simple items like coffee mugs and small plant pots.

This hobby has become deeply meaningful to me for a couple of key reasons. Firstly, it offers a wonderful creative outlet away from digital screens. Working with my hands requires absolute concentration, which helps me completely lose track of time and blow off steam after stressful workweeks. More importantly, pottery has taught me patience; clay is unforgiving, and when a pot collapses, you simply have to center yourself and begin anew. Taking home a finished, glazed cup that I crafted with my own hands gives me an immense sense of fulfillment.

p1.q: Do you have any hobbies that you prefer doing alone rather than with others?
p1.a: Definitely. I really enjoy sketching architectural buildings in my sketchbook by myself. It requires deep focus, and being alone allows me to immerse myself fully in the process without feeling self-conscious or distracted by conversation.

p1.q: Did you spend your leisure time differently when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, quite drastically. As a kid, I spent countless hours playing traditional street games with neighborhood friends, whereas nowadays my downtime revolves around solitary indoor pastimes like reading or listening to podcasts after tiring workdays.

p1.q: Is there a new hobby or creative pursuit you would like to take up soon?
p1.a: I would love to learn sourdough baking in the coming months. Crafting naturally fermented bread seems incredibly satisfying, and I really want to master the art of kneading dough to make fresh breakfasts at home.

p3.q: Why do some people find it difficult to maintain a regular hobby in modern society?
p3.a: In my opinion, the frantic pace of modern life is the main culprit. Many professionals juggle heavy workloads with domestic chores, leaving little mental energy for personal pursuits. Moreover, the prevalence of smartphones tempts people into passive entertainment like scrolling social media rather than actively cultivating a hobby. Consequently, meaningful leisure activities are often sidelined due to sheer cognitive fatigue and lack of disciplined schedule management.

p3.q: To what extent can hobbies influence an individual's personal or professional growth?
p3.a: I believe personal pastimes have a profound impact on one's development. Engaging in team sports or strategy games fosters critical soft skills like teamwork, problem-solving, and adaptability, which directly translate to the workplace. Furthermore, creative hobbies like painting or photography promote lateral thinking and emotional resilience. While some view leisure as unproductive downtime, it actually builds a well-rounded mindset that enhances professional competence over the long run.

hometown.sample:
A place in my hometown that I absolutely love visiting is West Lake, which is situated just a short ride north of Hanoi's bustling city center. It is an expansive freshwater lake surrounded by scenic tree-lined paths and lively open-air cafes.

Whenever I go there, there are plenty of enjoyable things to do. I usually like renting a bicycle to ride along the shoreline and feel the refreshing breeze, or simply grabbing an iced coffee with close friends at a lakeside cafe while watching the sunset paint the sky.

I tend to visit on weekend late afternoons, especially around dusk, because that is when the intense daytime heat subsides and the atmosphere turns genuinely tranquil. Occasionally, on exhausting weekdays, I also take a solitary stroll there in the evening to clear my head.

I truly cherish this spot because it provides a peaceful sanctuary away from the relentless traffic and chaos of the capital. The open water creates a rare sense of spaciousness, which helps me recharge my batteries and reflect on life.

p1.q: Where is your hometown?
p1.a: I was born and raised in Da Nang, a coastal city situated in central Vietnam. It is widely renowned for its scenic beaches like My Khe and iconic bridges stretching across the Han River.

p1.q: What do you like most about it?
p1.a: What I love most is the laid-back lifestyle alongside the welcoming locals. Despite its rapid modernisation, the local community remains exceptionally warm and always ready to lend a helping hand to newcomers.

p1.q: Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
p1.a: Yes, tremendously. In recent years, high-rise hotels and modern infrastructure have sprung up everywhere. While this economic boom has opened up countless career paths, it has also led to heavier traffic congestion during peak hours.

p3.q: Do you think young people want to stay in their hometowns?
p3.a: In my view, most ambitious youngsters nowadays prefer relocating to major metropolitan hubs rather than staying put. The primary catalyst is the vast array of lucrative employment options and modern educational facilities found in big cities. In contrast, smaller hometowns often lack specialised industries, leaving university graduates with fewer professional prospects. Nonetheless, some do eventually move back after gaining experience, seeking a calmer and more affordable lifestyle.

p3.q: How might tourism change a small town?
p3.a: Tourism brings a mixture of remarkable benefits and pronounced challenges to regional towns. On the positive side, it stimulates the local economy by creating jobs in hospitality and retail, often prompting local authorities to upgrade transport infrastructure. However, uncontrolled influxes of visitors frequently result in environmental degradation, inflated living costs, and the commercialisation of indigenous culture, which can gradually erode the town's unique local character.

Dùng sai thì khi mô tả sự biến đổi: Khi trả lời câu hỏi về sự thay đổi của quê hương, thí sinh hay dùng thì Quá khứ đơn thay vì thì Hiện tại hoàn thành (Present Perfect) để mô tả quá trình chuyển đổi kéo dài từ quá khứ đến nay.

Nhầm lẫn giữa 'hometown' và 'country': Nhiều bạn nhầm lẫn khi miêu tả quê hương bằng các dữ kiện của cả quốc gia (như diện tích Việt Nam, 54 dân tộc), trong khi 'hometown' chỉ giới hạn ở một thành phố, thị xã hoặc làng quê cụ thể.

housing.sample: If I could choose my dream home, it would be a contemporary two-storey villa nestled on the outskirts of Da Lat. This property would be tucked away in a tranquil residential area surrounded by pine trees, striking a balance between seclusion and convenience. Architecturally, it would embrace minimalist Scandinavian aesthetics, featuring floor-to-ceiling glass windows that flood the spacious interior with natural light and offer panoramic mountain views. Inside, the house would be fully equipped with all the mod cons, including an open-plan kitchen and a solar-powered heating system to keep the space cosy during chilly evenings. Outside, there would be a manicured backyard where I could cultivate herbs and sip my morning coffee. The main reason I would love to live there is the sense of serenity it provides. Life in metropolitan cities is becoming increasingly frantic, so having a peaceful retreat to unwind after demanding workdays would do wonders for my mental well-being. It wouldn’t just be a house; it would be a personal sanctuary where I could truly recharge.

p1.q: Do you live in a house or an apartment?
p1.a: Currently, I live in a modest high-rise apartment on the tenth floor. It’s quite compact, but it suits my lifestyle because it's within walking distance of my workplace and various grocery stores.

p1.q: What is your favourite room in your home?
p1.a: Undoubtedly my bedroom, because it’s my private sanctuary. I’ve decorated it with ambient lighting and indoor plants, so it’s the ideal spot to unwind with a good book after a long, hectic day.

p1.q: Would you like to move to a different home in the future?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. While my current flat is convenient, I hope to relocate to a standalone house with a small garden someday, primarily so my family can enjoy more privacy and fresh outdoor air.

p3.q: What are the main differences between living in a city apartment and living in a countryside house?
p3.a: In my view, the primary distinction lies in the trade-off between convenience and living space. City apartments offer immediate access to modern amenities, public transport, and commercial hubs, though residents often have to endure cramped conditions. Conversely, countryside houses provide generous living spaces and a serene environment, but everyday commuting and accessing specialized healthcare can be considerably more troublesome. Ultimately, it boils down to individual lifestyle priorities.

p3.q: How might housing designs change over the next few decades due to environmental challenges?
p3.a: I believe sustainable architecture will become the norm rather than a luxury. Faced with climate change and escalating energy costs, future dwellings are likely to integrate self-sufficient features such as solar-panel roofs, rainwater harvesting systems, and recycled insulation materials. In contrast to today’s carbon-heavy concrete blocks, upcoming houses will prioritize energy efficiency and climate resilience, helping urban populations reduce their ecological footprint substantially.

language-learning.sample: If I had the opportunity to pick up another foreign language, I would definitely choose Japanese. I've always been fascinated by Japanese culture, from its traditional arts to modern anime and gaming. To master it, my plan is to adopt a blended learning approach. Initially, I'd rely on language apps and podcasts to grasp the fundamentals of vocabulary and basic grammar. Afterwards, I would hire a native tutor online for weekly conversational practice to sharpen my speaking fluency. Of course, I know it won't be a walk in the park. The biggest hurdle will likely be mastering the complex writing systems, especially Kanji characters, which require immense memorization. Besides, Japanese honorifics and polite speech levels can be quite tricky for beginners. Nevertheless, I am keen on learning it because I want to travel across Japan without relying on translation apps, and perhaps even collaborate with Japanese partners in my future career. Experiencing a culture through its own tongue would be immensely rewarding.

p1.q: How many languages can you speak?
p1.a: Aside from my mother tongue, Vietnamese, I can speak English fluently. I use it every day for study and work, and I've also picked up a few basic Korean phrases from watching dramas.

p1.q: What do you find most challenging about learning a new language?
p1.a: I'd say mastering natural pronunciation and colloquial expressions is the hardest part. You can easily memorize grammar rules from textbooks, but sounding natural in everyday dialogue requires constant exposure and practice.

p1.q: Do you prefer learning a language independently or in a classroom?
p1.a: I prefer self-study because it allows me to progress at my own pace. Using podcasts and digital flashcards suits my schedule better than rigid classroom sessions, although classes are great for practicing speaking.

p3.q: Do you think artificial intelligence and translation tools will make language learning obsolete?
p3.a: I don't think automated tools will ever completely replace language learning. While AI can instantly translate texts and speech with impressive accuracy, it often misses cultural nuances, humor, and emotional depth. Furthermore, learning a language isn't just about exchanging practical information; it's about forming genuine human connections. Therefore, people will still want to speak foreign languages to build empathy and immerse themselves in different cultures.

p3.q: Why do children often pick up foreign languages more quickly than adults?
p3.a: In my view, children benefit from brain plasticity and an instinctive way of acquiring language through play and social interaction. Unlike adults, they are generally less self-conscious about making mistakes or mispronouncing words. In contrast, adults often overanalyze grammatical structures and feel anxious about sounding silly, which slows down their progress. Hence, an uninhibited mindset gives young learners a distinct advantage.

Dùng cách diễn đạt gượng gạo do dịch trực tiếp từ tiếng Việt, chẳng hạn nói 'talk English' thay vì 'speak English', hoặc 'know a language' thay vì 'achieve fluency in a language'.

Ý 2: Miêu tả phương pháp tiết kiệm cụ thể (thắt chặt chi tiêu, tự nấu ăn ở nhà, dùng ứng dụng theo dõi ngân sách cá nhân).
Kết: Bày tỏ niềm tự hào khi thanh toán bằng tiền tự tay làm ra và giá trị lâu dài mà thiết bị mang lại cho công việc.
money.sample: I would like to talk about a time when I saved up money to purchase a high-end laptop, specifically a MacBook Air, which I desperately needed for my university coursework and freelance design gigs. This happened roughly two years ago when my old computer abruptly gave up the ghost. The machine cost around one thousand dollars, which was a formidable sum for a student like me. It took me approximately six months of disciplined budgeting to amass that amount. To achieve this goal, I had to tighten my belt considerably. I took on extra evening tutoring shifts and made a conscious effort to prepare meals at home rather than eating out with friends. Every spare penny went straight into a dedicated savings fund so that I wouldn't be tempted to splurge. When I finally walked into the retail store and paid in full with my own hard-earned money, I felt an immense sense of pride. It wasn't merely a reliable work tool, but tangible proof that I could achieve a tough financial target through self-restraint.

p1.q: Do you prefer paying with cash or using digital payment methods?
p1.a: I definitely lean towards cashless options like mobile banking and digital wallets. They are incredibly convenient and save me from carrying bulky change, plus they automatically record my transactions, which makes budgeting effortless.

p1.q: Did you save money when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, I did. My parents gifted me a ceramic piggy bank where I regularly stored lucky money from New Year celebrations and spare change, which I later spent on storybooks.

p1.q: What kind of things do you usually spend most of your money on?
p1.a: The lion's share of my monthly budget goes towards essentials like groceries and public transit. Occasionally, I allocate some funds for online learning courses to develop my professional skill set.

p3.q: Why do some people find it difficult to manage their personal finances effectively?
p3.a: In my view, impulsive consumerism driven by targeted advertising and peer pressure is the main culprit. Many individuals live beyond their means just to project an affluent lifestyle on social media. Moreover, a widespread lack of budgeting education leaves people unable to plan for unforeseen expenses, eventually trapping them in vicious cycles of consumer debt.

p3.q: To what extent should financial literacy be taught as a compulsory subject in schools?
p3.a: I strongly believe that personal finance should be mandatory in the secondary school curriculum. While abstract subjects like calculus have merit, understanding taxation, compound interest, and debt management directly impacts every adult's quality of life. Teaching youngsters these practical competencies early produces responsible consumers and builds a far more financially resilient society overall.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai cấu trúc với động từ chỉ chi phí: người học hay nói 'I cost 50 dollars for this shirt' thay vì cấu trúc đúng là 'This shirt cost me 50 dollars' hoặc 'I spent 50 dollars on this shirt'.
Lạm dụng danh từ 'money' ở dạng số nhiều không chuẩn ('moneys') hoặc đi với lượng từ sai như 'many money' thay vì dùng 'a large amount of money' hay 'a lot of money'.

Thiếu các cách diễn đạt Band 7+ về tiền tệ, dẫn đến việc lặp đi lặp lại những từ cơ bản như 'cheap', 'expensive', 'buy' thay vì các cụm tự nhiên như 'budget-friendly', 'exorbitant', hoặc 'live within one's means'.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu bảo tàng bạn muốn kể (Bảo tàng Dân tộc học Việt Nam ở Hà Nội) và thời điểm ghé thăm gần đây.
Ý 1 (Nơi chốn & Người đồng hành): Nêu vị trí cụ thể ở quận Cầu Giấy và người bạn đi cùng vào dịp cuối tuần.
Ý 2 (Hiện vật trưng bày): Miêu tả trang phục thổ cẩm, nhạc cụ truyền thống và điểm nhấn là khu vườn kiến trúc ngoài trời với nhà rông, nhà dài.
Kết (Lý do ấn tượng): Giải thích trải nghiệm tương tác chân thực và cách bảo tàng tái hiện lịch sử sống động, sâu sắc hơn sách giáo khoa.
museums.sample: I would like to talk about the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology, located in the Cau Giay district of Hanoi. I visited it last autumn with one of my close friends who was in town for the weekend. The museum showcases the diverse cultural heritage of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups. Inside, there are thousands of everyday objects, elaborate tribal costumes, and traditional musical instruments on display. What really sets it apart, though, is the open-air architectural garden. It features full-scale replicas of traditional dwellings, such as the towering communal house of the Ba Na people and an authentic Ede longhouse. The reason this visit left such a lasting impression on me was how immersive the whole experience felt. Rather than keeping visitors behind velvet ropes, the museum offers a hands-on experience where you can step directly into the thatched houses and listen to audio recordings of traditional folk songs. It truly brought history to life and deepened my appreciation for the cultural richness of our country, making it far more memorable than any standard textbook lesson.

p1.q: Do you often visit museums or art galleries?
p1.a: To be honest, not very often, perhaps once or twice a year. I usually go when there is a special temporary exhibition in town, like the recent lacquer painting showcase at our local fine arts gallery.

p1.q: What kind of museums do you find most interesting?
p1.a: I am particularly drawn to interactive science museums. Rather than just staring at static objects behind glass, I love hands-on exhibits where you can press buttons, run small experiments, and see scientific concepts in action.

p1.q: Did you go to any museums when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. My elementary school organized annual field trips to the National History Museum. I vividly remember marveling at ancient stone tools and giant replica boats alongside all my classmates.

p3.q: Should public museums charge admission fees or be entirely free for citizens?
p3.a: In my view, public museums should ideally be free or charge only nominal fees. Since these institutions preserve shared cultural heritage, universal access ensures that people from all socio-economic backgrounds can benefit from educational resources. However, while relying on state funding is ideal, charging a small fee for special exhibits can help maintain preservation standards without alienating lower-income visitors. Balancing accessibility with financial sustainability is key.

p3.q: How might virtual museum tours change the way people appreciate cultural heritage in the future?
p3.a: Virtual tours are revolutionizing cultural engagement by democratizing access. Anyone with an internet connection can now explore global collections like the Louvre without paying for costly international flights. Nevertheless, high-resolution screens cannot completely replace the visceral emotional impact of standing in front of a real centuries-old masterpiece. Ultimately, virtual tours will serve as an enticing preview rather than a total substitute for genuine physical visits.

mistakesVi: Lặp từ 'museum' hoặc 'history' liên tục; nên luân chuyển linh hoạt bằng 'exhibition', 'cultural institution', 'gallery', hoặc 'heritage site'.
Dùng sai cụm cố định, ví dụ nói 'in display' thay vì 'on display', hoặc nhầm lẫn giữa 'artifact' (cổ vật nhân tạo) và 'antique' (đồ cổ thông thường).
Phát âm sai trọng âm của từ 'museum' (/mjuːˈziː.əm/), người học Việt Nam thường có xu hướng nhấn vào âm tiết đầu tiên thay vì âm tiết thứ hai.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu tên bài hát ('Fix You' của ban nhạc rock Coldplay), thể loại và vị trí đặc biệt của nó trong đời sống tinh thần của bạn.
Ý 1 (Khi nghe lần đầu): Kể hoàn cảnh nghe bài hát lần đầu vào giai đoạn ôn thi đại học căng thẳng, qua một chiếc tai nghe được bạn thân chia sẻ.
Ý 2 (Ý nghĩa): Giải thích thông điệp về sự kiên cường và an ủi vô điều kiện, nhắc nhở rằng vấp ngã là điều bình thường và hy vọng luôn ở phía trước.
Kết (Tại sao đặc biệt): Nhấn mạnh bài hát như một điểm tựa cảm xúc (emotional anchor) giúp xoa dịu áp lực và nhắc nhớ về tình bạn đẹp đẽ.
music.sample: I'd like to talk about 'Fix You' by the British rock band Coldplay, a song that holds a genuinely special place in my heart. I first stumbled upon it about five years ago during high school. It was an extremely stressful period because I was preparing for the grueling university entrance exams. One late afternoon in the school library, feeling thoroughly burnt out, my best friend handed me an earbud and pressed play. From the opening church organ chords to Chris Martin's gentle vocals, the track instantly struck a chord with me. The lyrics convey a message of unconditional support and resilience, reminding the listener that it's okay to falter and that hope will always guide you through dark times. What makes this song truly unique to me is that it acts as an emotional anchor. Whenever I experience setbacks at work or in my personal life, playing 'Fix You' helps me mellow out and puts things into perspective. More than just a piece of music, it serves as a comforting reminder of my friend's kindness and my own capacity to overcome hardships.

p1.q: What kind of music do you like?
p1.a: I have quite an eclectic taste, but I mostly lean towards indie pop and R&B. Upbeat melodies really lift my spirits, so I frequently listen to artists like Lauv or Daniel Caesar during my daily commute.

p1.q: Do you play any musical instruments?
p1.a: Honestly, I don't play any instruments because I'm virtually tone-deaf. I attempted to pick up the acoustic guitar a few years ago, but my clumsy fingers just couldn't master the chords, so I gave up.

p1.q: Do you listen to music when you study?
p1.a: Yes, but strictly instrumental tunes or lo-fi beats without lyrics. Songs with words tend to distract me, whereas ambient background music helps drown out surrounding noise and keeps me focused on challenging tasks.

p3.q: Why do people like different kinds of music?
p3.a: I believe musical preference is largely shaped by personality and cultural upbringing. For instance, energetic individuals often gravitate towards EDM or rock for stimulation, while introverted people might prefer classical or acoustic pieces to unwind. Additionally, the music we are exposed to during our teenage years creates deep emotional attachments. Therefore, diversity in personal experiences naturally leads to varied musical tastes.

p3.q: Should music be taught in all schools?
p3.a: Undoubtedly, yes. Music education fosters creativity and stimulates cognitive development in ways that traditional academic subjects cannot. For example, learning to read sheet music enhances spatial-temporal reasoning and mathematical thinking. Some argue that schools should focus exclusively on STEM subjects, but neglecting arts like music deprives children of a vital emotional outlet. Hence, it should definitely remain an integral part of the core curriculum.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai ngữ pháp với danh từ không đếm được: 'Music' là uncountable noun, người học thường quen miệng nói 'a music' hoặc 'many musics' thay vì 'a piece of music', 'a genre of music' hoặc dùng từ 'songs'.
Thiếu giới từ hoặc mạo từ: Rất nhiều thí sinh nói 'I often listen music' (thiếu 'to') hoặc 'I can play guitar' thay vì cụm chuẩn 'play the guitar' (nhạc cụ sau động từ play luôn cần mạo từ 'the').

Lạm dụng cách dịch thô từ tiếng Việt: Thường lặp đi lặp lại cụm 'relax my brain' hay 'relax my mind' (nghe gượng gạo trong tiếng Anh) thay vì dùng các cách diễn đạt tự nhiên như 'unwind', 'mellow out' hoặc 'take my mind off work'.

Ý 2 (Hoạt động & Bạn đồng hành): Kể lại chuyến đi cùng ai (bạn bè hoặc người thân) và những trải nghiệm thực tế (đi bộ đường dài, cắm trại dã ngoại).
Kết (Cảm nhận & Dấu ấn): Giải thích lý do nơi đây gây ấn tượng mạnh mẽ (giúp xua tan mệt mỏi nơi phố thị, tái tạo năng lượng tinh thần).
nature.sample: I'd like to share my experience visiting Ba Vi National Park, a stunning mountainous sanctuary nestled just outside Hanoi. I traveled there last autumn with a couple of close friends to take a weekend break from university life. The landscape was genuinely breathtaking, surrounded by mist-shrouded peaks and dense, lush greenery. As soon as we arrived, the cool, crisp mountain breeze felt like an instant breath of fresh air. We spent the morning trekking along winding stone trails, marveling at the rich flora and fauna and visiting an old French colonial church wrapped in moss. In the afternoon, we pitched a small tent near a pine forest and had a picnic while basking in the gentle sunlight. This trip made an indelible impression on me primarily because of the tranquil atmosphere. Living in a noisy concrete jungle, I constantly battle traffic and screen fatigue. Being able to commune with nature in such a serene environment completely recharged my mental batteries. It reminded me how vital untouched green spaces are for our emotional well-being.

p1.q: Do you often visit parks or botanical gardens?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. I make a habit of strolling through a nearby park every weekend morning to get some fresh air. It provides a peaceful retreat where I can stretch my legs and decompress after a hectic week.

p1.q: What do you usually like to do when you are in natural surroundings?
p1.a: I usually prefer brisk walking or simply sitting on a bench listening to natural sounds like birds chirping. Immersing myself in scenic landscapes helps clear my mind, especially when I listen to instrumental music on my headphones.

p1.q: Did you spend much time outdoors when you were a child?
p1.a: Yes, absolutely. Growing up in the countryside, I spent almost every afternoon playing football in open fields with neighborhood kids. We used to climb fruit trees and explore small streams, which kept us active and connected with nature.

p3.q: Why is it important for cities to incorporate public green spaces into urban planning?
p3.a: I believe urban green spaces are indispensable for both public health and environmental balance. Dense cities frequently suffer from severe air pollution and the urban heat island effect, which lush parks can actively mitigate by absorbing carbon dioxide. Moreover, these spaces offer residents essential recreational areas to exercise and socialize, significantly reducing stress levels compared to overcrowded indoor shopping malls. Therefore, green urban planning fosters healthier communities.

p3.q: How might modern technology affect younger generations' connection with the natural world?
p3.a: Undoubtedly, pervasive technology has created a widening gap between young people and the outdoors. Sedentary indoor habits, driven by video games and social media, often discourage teenagers from exploring natural parks. However, if used thoughtfully, digital tools like wildlife identification apps or nature vlogs can spark genuine curiosity about biodiversity. Ultimately, while screens pose an obvious distraction, they can also serve as educational catalysts if balanced properly.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng từ 'nature' sai ngữ pháp: Thường dùng nhầm 'nature park' thay vì 'natural park', hoặc quên mất 'nature' là danh từ không đếm được và không đi kèm mạo từ 'the' khi nói về thiên nhiên nói chung.
Lỗi phát âm các từ quen thuộc: Rất nhiều thí sinh phát âm sai trọng âm của từ 'atmosphere' (/ˈætməsfɪər/ nhấn âm 1) hoặc đọc sai nguyên âm của 'fauna' (/ˈfɔːnə/).

Diễn đạt ý quá đơn giản và lặp từ: Thường xuyên lặp lại cụm 'it makes me feel relaxed' thay vì dùng các cụm diễn đạt tự nhiên, giàu hình ảnh hơn như 'unwind', 'recharge my mental batteries' hay 'commune with nature'.

neighbours.sample:
I'd like to talk about Mr. Nam, a retired school principal who lives directly opposite my family's house. I first encountered him about three years ago during a weekend neighbourhood cleanup. While most residents were somewhat hesitant to participate, he took the initiative with great enthusiasm, which immediately left an impression on me.

Over the past few years, Mr. Nam has transformed our street into a truly vibrant and close-knit community. His most notable initiative was turning a neglected patch of vacant land at the corner of our alley into a flourishing communal herb garden. Besides that, he coordinated a weekly recycling program and routinely checks on elderly residents who live on their own.

I believe his efforts have made an extraordinary difference because he managed to break the ice among neighbours who previously barely exchanged greetings. Living in a bustling city often isolates people, yet his selflessness rekindled our shared civic spirit. Thanks to him, our neighbourhood feels noticeably safer, warmer, and far more connected than it ever was before.

p1.a: I know them quite well because we have lived on the same floor for five years. We often exchange homemade dishes during traditional holidays and occasionally stop for a friendly chat in the hallway.

p1.q: How often do you interact with your neighbours?
p1.a: I bump into them almost every day while waiting for the elevator or collecting parcels. On weekends, we sometimes grab morning coffee together at the local cafe just around the corner.

p1.q: Do you think it is important to have a good relationship with your neighbours?
p1.a: Definitely, because neighbours are the closest support network in times of emergency. For instance, when my pipes burst last winter, my adjacent neighbour immediately lent me tools and helped shut off the main valve.

p3.q: In what ways has urbanisation changed the relationship between neighbours in modern cities?
p3.a: Urbanisation has undeniably fostered anonymity. In high-rise apartment complexes, busy work schedules and private lifestyle choices mean that residents often keep to themselves, rarely knowing who lives next door. In contrast to rural hamlets where doors remain wide open, urban living prioritises privacy over communal solidarity, leading to weaker interpersonal bonds in metropolitan areas.

p3.q: To what extent should local governments encourage neighbourhood bonding activities?
p3.a: In my opinion, authorities ought to facilitate communal engagement rather than mandate it. By funding community centres or hosting green living workshops, councils can provide fertile ground for spontaneous interactions. However, participation must remain strictly voluntary, since over-regulating neighbourhood life could alienate citizens who value personal downtime after demanding working weeks.

news.sample:
A few weeks ago, while browsing a science journalism website, I stumbled across a truly fascinating piece of breaking news about a breakthrough in environmental engineering. The report highlighted an autonomous solar-powered vessel designed by a group of young Dutch engineers to capture plastic debris in rivers before it reaches the open ocean.

What caught my attention immediately was the practical ingenuity of the invention. Rather than deploying massive vessels that consume heavy fossil fuels, this system operates entirely on renewable energy and runs round the clock with minimal human intervention. Furthermore, initial trial runs in Southeast Asia showed that it could extract tons of synthetic waste within days.

I found this news extraordinarily encouraging. In an era dominated by alarming headlines about global warming and ecological crises, hearing about tangible, practical solutions felt like a breath of fresh air. It filled me with genuine optimism about our ability to reverse ecological damage through innovation, and it even inspired me to be more conscious of my own single-use plastic consumption.

p1.q: How do you usually get your daily news?
p1.a: I predominantly get my news through digital news aggregator apps on my smartphone. They provide concise digests and real-time alerts from reputable publishers, which fits neatly into my busy morning commute.

p1.q: Do you prefer reading international news or domestic news?
p1.a: I lean towards international news because I'm fascinated by global geopolitics and economic trends. However, I still glance through local headlines daily to stay informed about community developments and domestic public policies.

p1.q: Did you follow the news much when you were younger?
p1.a: Not really, as I found conventional newspapers rather tedious and abstract as a child. I mostly watched cartoons, only catching glimpses of the evening television news when my parents had it on.

p3.q: Why do many people prefer getting news from social media rather than traditional newspapers?
p3.a: Social media platforms offer immediacy and personalized algorithmic feeds that conventional newspapers simply cannot rival. Users receive bite-sized updates within seconds of an incident, accompanied by interactive commentary. However, this convenience often comes at the expense of journalistic rigor and objective fact-checking, making users vulnerable to sensationalism. Nonetheless, the fast-paced nature of modern life drives audiences toward these instant digital streams.

p3.q: To what extent should governments regulate fake news on digital platforms?
p3.a: In my view, state intervention is necessary to curb malicious misinformation, especially regarding public health or civil safety. Unchecked falsehoods can easily incite panic and erode social trust. Nevertheless, strict state oversight risks sliding into censorship and suppressing legitimate dissent. Therefore, rather than outright bans, authorities should mandate algorithmic transparency from tech giants while investing heavily in citizens' media literacy.

Lỗi diễn đạt thô: Dịch nguyên xi từ tiếng Việt 'xem tin tức trên tivi/mạng' thành 'see news' thay vì sử dụng các collocation tự nhiên như 'watch the news', 'read the news', hoặc 'follow current affairs'.

photography.sample: I would like to talk about a memorable photograph I took roughly two years ago during a summer holiday on Phu Quoc island with my closest friends. It was taken late in the afternoon on a tranquil stretch of beach. The photo captured three of my companions leaping into the air against a blazing orange sunset, creating a striking silhouette effect as gentle waves broke around their feet. At the time, I didn't own a high-end camera, so I simply relied on my smartphone. However, I lowered the exposure slightly and fired off a burst of candid shots right during the golden hour to freeze their figures mid-air. The composition turned out remarkably well, with golden reflections shimmering across the wet sand. This picture holds immense sentimental value for me because it was our final trip together before two of them moved abroad for their master's degrees. Whenever life gets overwhelming, glancing at that snapshot instantly evokes fond memories of our youth and reminds me of a bond that remains unbroken despite the physical distance.

p1.q: Do you enjoy taking photos in your daily life?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. I love taking candid shots of spontaneous moments, like an impromptu coffee with friends or an unusual sunset. It is an effortless way to document daily life without having to write a diary.

p1.q: How often do you look back at old photographs?
p1.a: I usually scroll through my cloud gallery every couple of months, especially when I feel nostalgic. Looking at old snapshots always brings back warm memories and shows me how much my life has evolved.

p1.q: Do you prefer taking photos with a smartphone or a digital camera?
p1.a: I lean towards smartphones because of sheer convenience. While a digital camera produces superior image quality, modern phone cameras are remarkably advanced and allow me to capture fleeting moments instantly without carrying heavy lenses.

p3.q: Why do some people prefer to capture moments on camera rather than simply enjoying them in the present?
p3.a: I believe many people focus on their lenses out of an anxiety about forgetting precious milestones. Photographs offer tangible proof of an experience that can be revisited or shared on social media later. However, obsessing over getting the perfect shot often detracts from genuine presence, causing individuals to view events as mere content rather than living them fully. Balancing both is crucial.

p3.q: How has digital photography altered the way society preserves history and memories?
p3.a: Digital technology has democratized photography, meaning virtually anyone can document historical shifts or everyday life in real time. Unlike fragile printed albums, digital archives store vast volumes effortlessly. On the flip side, this sheer abundance often devalues individual images; people take thousands of throwaway snapshots that are rarely revisited, whereas physical photographs in the past carried deeper emotional weight and permanence.

reading.sample:
I would like to talk about Atomic Habits, an inspiring personal development book written by James Clear. It centers around the profound idea that making tiny, incremental improvements in our daily routines can compound into remarkable life changes over time.

I picked up this book about two years ago during my final year at university. Back then, I was struggling with chronic procrastination and feeling constantly overwhelmed by assignment deadlines, so I desperately needed a practical framework to regain discipline.

What sets this book apart is Clear's accessible and evidence-based approach. Rather than relying on vague motivational clichés, he offers tangible concepts such as habit stacking and environmental redesign. I personally applied his 'two-minute rule' to build a consistent study schedule, which genuinely transformed my productivity and mindset.

I would wholeheartedly recommend this book to anyone striving for self-improvement. It is not just an entertaining read, but an invaluable toolkit that provides practical solutions for breaking bad habits and achieving long-term goals.

p1.q: Do you like reading?
p1.a: Yes, absolutely. I consider myself an avid reader because diving into a good book helps me decompress after hectic work hours. For instance, I always set aside thirty minutes before bed to read fiction.

p1.q: What kind of books do you read?
p1.a: I have fairly eclectic tastes, but I lean heavily towards non-fiction, particularly psychology and memoirs. Occasionally, I pick up detective stories like Sherlock Holmes just to keep my analytical thinking sharp and entertained.

p1.q: Do you prefer reading on paper or on a screen?
p1.a: I definitely prefer physical paper books. There is an irreplaceable charm to turning real pages and feeling paper textures. In contrast, staring at digital screens for hours tends to strain my eyes and cause fatigue.

p3.q: Are printed books going to disappear?
p3.a: I highly doubt paper books will ever vanish entirely. Even though e-books offer unmatched portability and instant accessibility, physical books carry an emotional and tactile value that screens simply cannot replicate. Many people take genuine pride in curating home bookshelves. Therefore, while digital reading will certainly hold a dominant share, printed volumes will endure as treasured keepsakes.

p3.q: Should children be encouraged to read fiction?
p3.a: Without a doubt, children ought to be actively encouraged to explore fictional stories. Reading fiction sparks creativity and helps young minds develop empathy by walking in the shoes of diverse characters. For example, imaginative tales like Harry Potter teach resilience and friendship far more vividly than dry textbooks. Ultimately, fiction cultivates emotional depth and a lifelong passion for learning.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai cụm từ 'read book': Thí sinh thường dịch nguyên văn tiếng Việt thành 'I like read book' hoặc 'I read book every day'. Danh từ đếm được 'book' phải ở dạng số nhiều ('read books') hoặc dùng danh động từ 'reading'.

Lạm dụng từ 'novel' cho mọi thể loại sách: Nhiều bạn gọi cả sách kỹ năng, sách khoa học hay sách giáo khoa là 'novel'. Cần phân biệt rõ: 'novel' chỉ dành riêng cho tiểu thuyết hư cấu, còn thể loại chung là 'book' hoặc 'non-fiction'.
