safety.sample: I would like to talk about an incident from about two years ago when I genuinely feared for my personal safety. It occurred late one evening while I was walking back to my apartment after finishing an overtime shift. The bus dropped me off on the main boulevard, but reaching my flat required navigating a poorly lit residential alleyway. As I entered the alley, I noticed heavy footsteps tailing me. When I accelerated my pace, the silhouette behind me matched my speed. Realizing I was a vulnerable target in such a deserted area, my heart raced and I was immediately on high alert. Instead of freezing up, I took immediate precautionary measures. I grabbed my phone, pretended to be on an urgent call with my brother, and announced my exact location loudly. Spotting a 24-hour convenience store just ahead, I swiftly darted inside and stood beside the cashier counter. After waiting there for fifteen minutes, I saw the person pass by and disappear. A tremendous sense of relief washed over me, and that close call taught me never to take personal safety for granted.

p1.q: Do you feel safe walking alone in your neighborhood at night?
p1.a: Yes, I do, because my area has bright streetlights and active neighborhood patrols. However, I still avoid isolated backstreets late at night just to err on the side of caution.

p1.q: What do you usually do to keep your personal belongings safe when traveling?
p1.a: I always keep my passport and wallet in a concealed crossbody pouch worn in front of me. This simple habit keeps opportunistic pickpockets at bay, especially in crowded railway stations.

p1.q: Have you ever witnessed or reported a minor crime?
p1.a: Yes, once at a night market, I saw a thief attempt to snatch a backpack. I immediately alerted the nearby security guards, who responded swiftly and apprehended the suspect.

p3.q: Do you think installing more surveillance cameras in public places effectively deters criminal activities?
p3.a: In my view, widespread CCTV networks serve as an invaluable deterrent to street crime. When individuals realize their identities and actions are recorded in real time, they are far less inclined to commit illicit acts like vandalism or robbery. However, cameras cannot stop every crime, so regular foot patrols by police officers remain equally vital.

p3.q: How might advancements in digital technology change the types of crimes committed in the future?
p3.a: Technology is steadily shifting offenses from physical streets to the digital realm. Ý 2 (Cách thực hiện): Miêu tả căn phòng tối, khe hẹp cho tia sáng mặt trời đi qua lăng kính thủy tinh và tán sắc trên bức tường trắng.

science.sample: I would like to talk about Isaac Newton's famous prism experiment, which completely revolutionized our understanding of light. I first encountered it during a middle school physics class when our teacher brought a triangular glass prism into the laboratory. The setup was remarkably simple yet profound. Our teacher darkened the entire classroom, made a tiny pinhole in the window blind to let a single narrow beam of sunlight penetrate, and placed the prism right in its path. Instantly, the ray of white light refracted and fanned out into a vibrant spectrum of seven distinct colours across the far wall, creating an artificial rainbow. What fascinated me even more was when he placed a second, inverted prism right after the first, recombining those colourful rays back into pure white light. This demonstration blew my mind because it disproved the prevailing belief that colour was merely an alteration of light caused by darkness. Instead, it provided undeniable empirical evidence that white light is actually a composite of all spectral colours. It completely demystified everyday natural phenomena like rainbows and ignited my lifelong curiosity about physical science.

p1.q: Did you enjoy learning science subjects when you were in school?
p1.a: To be honest, I was really keen on biology because our teacher often let us examine plant cells under microscopes, which felt magical. However, I struggled quite a bit with theoretical physics and complicated mathematical formulas.

p1.q: What area of science do you find most interesting nowadays?
p1.a: I'm genuinely drawn to neuroscience at the moment. It is deeply fascinating to explore how neural pathways affect our daily habits, cognitive functions, and emotional responses, especially through science podcasts hosted by academic experts.

p1.q: Do you often watch science documentaries or read science news?
p1.a: Yes, fairly regularly. Whenever I have some downtime on weekends, I enjoy watching astronomy and wildlife documentaries on streaming platforms because they are visually breathtaking and present complex discoveries in an accessible, engaging format.

p3.q: To what extent should scientific research be funded by the government rather than private corporations?
p3.a: In my view, fundamental and life-saving research must predominantly receive public funding. While private corporations bring capital and operational speed, their primary driver is commercial profit, which often sidelines non-remunerative sectors such as rare disease therapies. In contrast, government-sponsored research protects scientific objectivity and ensures discoveries remain accessible public goods. Therefore, while corporate collaboration is valuable, public oversight is vital.

p3.q: How can schools encourage more young people, especially girls, to pursue careers in science?
p3.a: Schools ought to abandon passive textbook memorization and introduce interactive, project-based laboratory work from an early age. Moreover, actively showcasing female role models, such as inviting women working in aerospace engineering or biotechnology for guest lectures, can dismantle persistent gender stereotypes. When young girls interact with relatable mentors, their confidence increases, fostering long-term interest in STEM careers.

shopping.sample: I’d like to talk about a pair of noise-cancelling headphones I bought about six months ago, which turned out to be one of the best investments I’ve ever made. At the time, I was working remotely from home and frequently studying at bustling coffee shops. The ambient noise made it really difficult to concentrate, so I desperately needed a decent gadget to tune out distractions. After doing some research and reading countless customer reviews, I decided to splash out on a Sony model. I bought it online via an e-commerce platform during their mid-year mega sale. I was lucky enough to apply several discount vouchers, so I snapped it up at a bargain price. I’m genuinely thrilled with this purchase for several reasons. Firstly, the sound quality is top-notch, and the active noise-cancellation works like a charm. It creates a serene bubble wherever I am, boosting my productivity immensely. On top of that, the battery life lasts for days, proving that it offers fantastic value for money. It has honestly become an indispensable part of my daily routine.

p1.q: Do you like shopping?
p1.a: To be honest, I'm quite fond of shopping, especially when I need some retail therapy after a hectic week. Browsing through clothes or gadgets gives me a quick mood boost, though I try not to overspend.

p3.q: Do advertisements make people buy things they do not need?
p3.a: Undoubtedly, yes. Modern advertisements employ sophisticated psychological tactics and influencer endorsements to create a sense of urgency and false necessity. For example, flash sales and limited-edition claims often trigger impulse buys, prompting consumers to purchase trendy apparel or gadgets they rarely use. Consequently, people end up wasting substantial amounts of money on non-essential items just to keep up with short-lived lifestyle trends.

p3.q: Will shops disappear in the future?
p3.a: I don't think physical stores will vanish entirely, though their roles will certainly transform. While e-commerce dominates convenience and speed, brick-and-mortar shops offer tangible experiences that screens cannot replicate, such as trying on tailored clothes or testing perfume. Therefore, rather than disappearing, retail shops will likely evolve into experiential showrooms where customers interact with products before purchasing.

sleep.sample: I'd like to talk about a night when I could barely get any shut-eye, which happened about a year ago right before my university thesis defense. I was staying in my small rented room in Hanoi during a sweltering summer heatwave. What kept me awake was a toxic combination of physical discomfort and intense psychological anxiety. The room felt like an oven because my air conditioner had malfunctioned, and every time I tried to drift off, my mind raced with worst-case scenarios about stumbling over my presentation. To induce sleep, I tried drinking warm water, reading a dense textbook, and playing ambient rain sounds, but nothing seemed to quiet my racing thoughts. I spent hours tossing and turning, repeatedly checking the glowing alarm clock. By sunrise, I had managed perhaps an hour of restless dozing. The next morning, I felt completely drained and lightheaded, with a pounding headache and stinging eyes. I had to chug a double espresso just to stay upright. Fortunately, the defense went well, but that grueling experience taught me that catastrophic thinking before bedtime is entirely counterproductive.

p1.q: How many hours of sleep do you usually get each night?
p1.a: I typically get around seven hours of uninterrupted rest. On weekdays, I try to turn in by eleven so that I can wake up refreshed at six for my morning jog, though tight deadlines occasionally cut that short.

p1.q: Do you ever take naps during the middle of the day?
p1.a: Yes, I regularly take a twenty-minute power nap right after lunch. It recharges my mental batteries effectively, preventing the dreaded mid-afternoon slump and keeping my focus sharp until the workday finishes.

p3.q: How has modern technology altered people's sleeping habits in recent years?
p3.a: In my view, modern tech has severely compromised global sleep patterns. Digital screens emit blue light that suppresses melatonin, which delays our body's natural sleep signals. Furthermore, social media algorithms encourage mindless scrolling late into the night. While our ancestors woke and slept with the sun, contemporary society treats rest as optional, creating widespread sleep deficits and chronic exhaustion.

p3.q: Should employers encourage their staff to take short naps during the workday?
p3.a: I firmly believe they should, because midday naps directly boost cognitive stamina and creative problem-solving. A brief twenty-minute rest restores concentration and substantially minimizes costly workplace errors. While conservative managers may equate napping with laziness, progressive tech corporations have proven that designated nap spaces actually yield higher daily productivity and job satisfaction, creating mutual benefits for both sides.

I usually check their channel every couple of weeks whenever a notification pops up, and I rarely miss a single upload. I also occasionally join the comment section to read different perspectives from viewers around the globe. What makes this channel truly stand out is how it manages to make serious education feel entertaining. In an era where social media is flooded with shallow clickbait, Kurzgesagt provides genuine substance. Every video leaves me with a renewed sense of curiosity about the universe, and I honestly think it represents the very best of what online media can offer.

Ý 1 (Ở đâu & Với ai): Chọn học tại một bờ biển có sóng êm như Đà Nẵng; rủ một người bạn thân có chung sở thích phiêu lưu tham gia một khóa học ngắn hạn với huấn luyện viên chuyên nghiệp.
Ý 2 (Quá trình tập luyện): Bắt đầu từ việc tập giữ thăng bằng trên bãi cát, học cách đọc hướng sóng, rồi chèo ván ra xa bờ và trải nghiệm cảm giác ngã xuống nước trước khi đứng vững.
Kết: Giải thích lý do muốn học (rèn luyện sức bền toàn thân, vượt qua nỗi sợ nước sâu và hòa mình vào thiên nhiên); nêu dự định thực hiện vào mùa hè tới.
sport.sample:
If I had the chance to pick up a new sport, I would definitely go for surfing. It has always fascinated me because of the thrilling combination of athleticism and a deep connection with nature.

Ideally, I would love to take lessons in Da Nang, where the coastline offers consistent, beginner-friendly waves. I wouldn't want to tackle this alone, so I would invite my close friend Minh, who is also a thrill-seeker, to join a week-long surf camp with certified instructors.

Surfing appeals to me for a couple of key reasons. Firstly, it provides an intense full-body workout, demanding core strength, balance, and quick reflexes. Navigating the waves seems like an incredible way to build stamina and get into shape. More importantly, I want to conquer my mild fear of deep water and step outside my comfort zone. There is something deeply empowering about riding a wave and feeling the raw power of the ocean beneath your board.

Hopefully, I can make this plan a reality next summer, as it would be both a rewarding physical challenge and an unforgettable adventure.

p1.q: Do you play any sports?
p1.a: Yes, I play badminton quite regularly. I usually meet up with some colleagues twice a week at a local sports hall. It is an accessible game that keeps me active and helps me unwind after long hours at my desk.

p1.q: Do you prefer watching or playing sport?
p1.a: I definitely lean towards playing rather than watching. Being actively involved lets me blow off steam and work up a sweat, whereas sitting in front of a screen cheering for teams often feels passive and unproductive.

p1.q: How often do you exercise?
p1.a: I try to work out around three to four times a week. My routine typically involves thirty-minute jogging sessions in the nearby park or quick home workouts to maintain my cardiovascular health and keep my energy levels high.

p3.q: Should schools spend more money on sport?
p3.a: I firmly believe schools should allocate a larger budget to sports facilities and physical education. Regular exercise improves students' focus and combats rising adolescent obesity rates. For instance, well-equipped gyms and pitches encourage even reluctant pupils to stay active. While academic subjects are undeniably vital, neglecting sports can lead to severe sedentary habits. Therefore, balanced investment is crucial for both mental sharpness and physical well-being.

p3.q: Why do some people never exercise?
p3.a: The primary culprit is usually a perceived lack of time due to demanding work schedules and domestic responsibilities. Many modern professionals feel utterly drained by evening, so they opt for sedentary leisure like scrolling on phones instead. Additionally, some people find exercise tedious because they haven't discovered an activity they genuinely enjoy. Without intrinsic motivation or a supportive peer group, maintaining a consistent fitness habit becomes remarkably difficult.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai động từ kết hợp (Collocation: play / do / go): Người học hay nói 'play yoga' hoặc 'play swimming' thay vì đúng chuẩn là 'do yoga' (cho các bài tập cá nhân/võ thuật) và 'go swimming' (cho các môn đuôi -ing). Nhớ quy tắc: môn có bóng/thi đấu dùng 'play'.

Dịch nguyên từ tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh thiếu tự nhiên: Hay nói 'sport makes me healthy' hoặc 'sport gives me good health' thay vì dùng các cụm Band 7+ như 'stay in shape', 'boost my physical well-being', hay 'keep fit'.

outlineVi: Mở đầu: Giới thiệu môn Hóa học hữu cơ (Organic Chemistry) vào năm cuối cấp ba là môn học bản thân từng rất chật vật.
Ý 1 - Vì sao khó: Kiến thức trừu tượng, hàng trăm cơ chế phản ứng phức tạp đòi hỏi tư duy không gian thay vì chỉ học vẹt; từng trượt bài thi giữa kỳ đầu tiên.
Ý 2 - Cách cải thiện: Lập sơ đồ tư duy (mind maps) để liên kết phản ứng, tham gia nhóm học tập sau giờ học và xem các video bài giảng 3D trên mạng.
Kết - Cảm nhận hiện tại: Dù không theo đuổi ngành khoa học, trải nghiệm này giúp rèn luyện tính kiên trì và chứng minh rằng thử thách nào cũng có thể vượt qua nếu nỗ lực.
studies.sample: To be completely honest, the most challenging subject I ever tackled was advanced chemistry during my final year of high school. At first, I felt completely out of my depth. Unlike general science, organic chemistry had a remarkably steep learning curve. It involved memorizing countless intricate reaction mechanisms and visualizing abstract molecular structures in three dimensions. I remember failing my very first midterm test, which was a huge wake-up call for me. Determined not to fall behind, I completely changed my study habits. Instead of relying on rote learning, I started drawing detailed mind maps to connect different reactions logically. I also joined a peer study group after class where we took turns explaining complex problems to each other, and I spent weekends watching visual chemistry tutorials on YouTube. Eventually, my efforts paid off, and I managed to secure a solid grade in the final examination. Looking back, while I never pursued a career in science, conquering such a daunting subject taught me resilience and critical thinking. It showed me that even the toughest intellectual obstacles can be overcome with persistence and the right approach.

p1.q: What do you study at the moment?
p1.a: Right now, I'm pursuing a bachelor's degree in international business at university. I chose this field because I'm fascinated by global trade, and my coursework involves practical modules like market analysis and cross-cultural negotiations.

p1.q: Did you enjoy school when you were younger?
p1.a: Yes, I really loved my school days. Beyond the academic side, school provided a vibrant social environment where I forged lifelong friendships, especially through extracurricular activities like playing football and participating in the school choir.

p1.q: Which subject is the most useful, in your opinion?
p1.a: In my view, mathematics is by far the most practical subject. It fosters analytical reasoning and logical problem-solving, which are indispensable skills in everyday life, whether you're managing personal finances or analyzing market trends.

p3.q: Should students be able to choose all their subjects?
p3.a: I don't think students should have total freedom in choosing all their subjects. While having autonomy fosters genuine enthusiasm, foundational subjects like mathematics, basic science, and native language literacy are vital for everyday life. For instance, without mandatory math, teenagers might opt out of numeracy skills essential for future employment. Therefore, a balanced curriculum combining core compulsory subjects with elective courses is a far healthier approach.

p3.q: How has learning changed because of technology?
p3.a: Technology has revolutionized education by making knowledge instantly accessible and highly interactive. In the past, students were confined to textbooks and teacher-led lectures, whereas today, learners can access online courses, video tutorials, and AI tutors from anywhere globally. For instance, platforms like Coursera allow self-paced study across diverse fields. Consequently, education has transitioned from passive absorption to self-directed, flexible learning.

mistakesVi: Dùng sai động từ: Thường nhầm lẫn giữa 'learn' và 'study' (ví dụ: nói 'I learn Business at university' thay vì 'I am studying/majoring in Business').

Nhầm lẫn thì động từ: Khi trả lời Part 2 về môn học trong quá khứ, thí sinh hay chuyển đổi lộn xộn giữa quá khứ đơn và hiện tại đơn ('I study this because it is hard' thay vì 'I studied this because it was hard').
Dùng sai giới từ trong cụm học thuật: Nói 'good in math' thay vì 'good at math', hoặc 'graduate university' thay vì 'graduate from university'.

teachers.sample: I would like to talk about Mr. Hoang, my high school English teacher who made a profound impact on my educational journey. I attended his classes during tenth grade at a public secondary school in Hanoi. Back then, English felt like a chore filled with dry grammar exercises. However, Mr. Hoang transformed that perception completely. Instead of relying on rote memorization, he tailored his teaching methods by introducing debate sessions, pop songs, and movie scripts into the curriculum. He was exceptionally patient and approachable, which encouraged even the most introverted students to speak up without fear of making mistakes. What made him unique was his dedication to leading by example; whenever we struggled with academic writing, he spent hours offering personalized feedback rather than merely pointing out grammatical errors. He had such a lasting influence on me because he instilled a genuine passion for foreign languages that persists today. Thanks to his constant encouragement, I built the confidence to pursue international studies, which fundamentally altered my career direction.

p1.q: Do you remember your first teacher from primary school?
p1.a: Yes, vividly. Her name was Mrs. Lan, and she taught my first-grade class. She was exceptionally gentle and patient, which completely eased my anxiety when I was terrified of being separated from my parents.

p1.q: What qualities do you think make a good teacher?
p1.a: In my view, empathy and enthusiasm are paramount. A great instructor does not just impart knowledge, but actively connects with learners and stimulates curiosity, much like my high school literature teacher did.

p1.q: Would you ever consider becoming a teacher in the future?
p1.a: Honestly, no, because I lack the patience required for effective classroom management. Educating energetic teenagers demands extraordinary resilience, which I observed firsthand while watching my mother work as a high school instructor.

p3.q: How has the role of teachers changed with the rise of modern educational technology?
p3.a: I believe teachers have transitioned from being the sole distributors of information to facilitators of active learning. Historically, students relied almost exclusively on teacher lectures and textbooks, whereas today, online platforms and artificial intelligence offer instantaneous answers. Consequently, modern educators must concentrate on teaching students how to critically evaluate sources and solve problems collaboratively, ensuring technology enhances rather than replaces human mentorship.

p3.q: Should teachers be primarily responsible for teaching academic subjects or moral values to children?
p3.a: I believe both dimensions are essential, but moral development should not rest entirely on teachers. While educators must definitely model ethical behavior and integrity at school, parents remain the foundational role models for a child's character. If schools carry the full burden of moral upbringing alongside rigid academic syllabuses, pedagogical quality inevitably declines. Therefore, a shared partnership between families and institutions is imperative.

Lạm dụng các tính từ quá chung chung và đơn giản như 'good', 'kind', 'friendly' thay vì sử dụng từ vựng chỉ kỹ năng sư phạm như 'dedicated', 'approachable', 'inspiring'.

technology.sample: I'd like to talk about my robotic vacuum cleaner, a gadget that has genuinely transformed my daily routine. I purchased it about two years ago when I moved into my own apartment and found myself completely swamped with work, leaving little time for household chores. This little device is an absolute game-changer. It automatically maps out my floor plan and navigates around furniture to sweep and mop every single day. I can easily schedule cleanings via a mobile app, meaning I often return home to spotless floors without lifting a finger. It has freed up at least three to four hours a week, allowing me to unwind or focus on my studies instead of constantly dusting. That being said, it isn't entirely flawless. One minor drawback is that it occasionally gets trapped in stray charging cables or thick carpets, which means I have to untangle it manually. Also, replacement filters and maintenance can be quite pricey over time. Nevertheless, the sheer convenience it provides far outweighs these trivial hassles, and I can hardly imagine my life without it.

p1.q: How often do you use your phone?
p1.a: Practically around the clock. Aside from sleeping, I constantly check it for work emails, messaging apps, and navigation. For instance, I use Google Maps almost every morning to dodge traffic jams on my way to the office.

p1.q: What do you use your phone for most?
p1.a: Mainly for productivity and communication. I handle team chats on Slack and organize my schedule via digital calendars. In fact, without these apps, keeping up with daily project deadlines would be nearly impossible.

p1.q: Do you think people rely on technology too much?
p1.a: Definitely. Many of us have become overly dependent on gadgets for basic tasks. For example, hardly anyone memorizes phone numbers or navigates without GPS nowadays, which shows how our cognitive skills are taking a back seat.

p3.q: Does technology make people less social?
p3.a: In my view, it's a double-edged sword. On one hand, social media and messaging platforms allow us to stay connected across long distances. However, in real life, face-to-face interactions are noticeably dwindling because people are glued to their screens, even during dinner parties. So while we may appear more virtually connected, our meaningful, in-person social bonds are definitely weakening.

p3.q: What technology do you think will be common in 20 years?
p3.a: I believe autonomous vehicles and advanced artificial intelligence will become part of everyday life. Currently, self-driving cars are still in testing phases and quite costly, but in two decades, they could completely replace human drivers to reduce road accidents. Ultimately, AI assistants will likely manage everything from domestic chores to complex workplace decisions seamlessly.

Phát âm sai trọng âm của các từ cơ bản: Từ 'technology' nhấn âm 2 (/tekˈnɒl.ə.dʒi/) thường bị phát âm sai thành 'tếch-nô-lô-di', hoặc 'device' (/dɪˈvaɪs/) bị đọc thành 'đê-vít'.

time-management.sample:
I would like to talk about time-blocking, a scheduling technique that has truly transformed my daily productivity. I first adopted this habit during my sophomore year at university, when I felt completely overwhelmed by overlapping coursework, part-time shifts, and club commitments. Because I was constantly burning the candle at both ends, I knew I needed a more disciplined approach.

Basically, every Sunday evening, I divide my upcoming week into dedicated ninety-minute blocks on my digital calendar. Instead of keeping a chaotic to-do list, I allocate specific slots for academic research, drafting assignments, and personal workouts. During each designated block, I silence my phone notifications to enter a state of deep concentration.

This method works remarkably well for me because it eliminates decision fatigue. Rather than wondering what to do next, I simply follow my prearranged schedule. Furthermore, it sets clear boundaries so that professional tasks do not bleed into my evenings. Ultimately, this habit enables me to meet tight deadlines effortlessly while striking a genuinely healthy balance in my everyday routine.

p1.q: Do you usually plan your day in advance?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. Every evening, I jot down my top three priorities for the following day on my phone. This simple routine keeps me focused and stops me from getting overwhelmed by unexpected distractions.

p1.q: What do you find most difficult about managing your time?
p1.a: I think resisting digital interruptions is the hardest part. It is far too tempting to procrastinate by checking social media while writing reports, which frequently throws my planned schedule off track.

p1.q: Did you learn how to manage your time when you were a child?
p1.a: Not in any formal sense, but my parents always insisted that I finish homework before playing outside. That strict rule gradually instilled in me the essential habit of putting duties before leisure.

p3.q: Why do some people struggle to balance their work commitments and personal life nowadays?
p3.a: I believe constant digital connectivity is the main culprit. With mobile apps like Slack and email synced to smartphones, employers frequently demand immediate replies outside office hours. As a result, the boundary between professional tasks and private downtime has blurred. Unless professionals consciously unplug in the evenings, achieving genuine work-life balance remains virtually impossible.

p3.q: To what extent can digital tools improve personal productivity compared to traditional paper planners?
p3.a: Digital tools offer clear advantages through automated notifications, cross-device syncing, and effortless rescheduling. For example, shared calendars prevent overlapping meetings in corporate environments. That said, paper planners retain substantial value because handwriting fosters mindfulness and clearer cognitive retention. Therefore, combining both formats often yields the most sustainable productivity.

transport.sample: I'd like to share an unforgettable experience I had aboard the Reunification Express train journeying from Hanoi down to Da Nang last summer. I took this scenic overnight trip alongside two of my closest university friends after finishing our final semester. We boarded a sleeper carriage at twilight, and as the locomotive pulled away, the bustling urban sprawl gradually gave way to tranquil countryside vistas. What truly made this trip extraordinary was traversing the iconic Hai Van Pass the following morning. Sitting by the panoramic window with a warm cup of coffee, I was mesmerised by dramatic misty cliffs on one side and the shimmering turquoise ocean directly below. Unlike the rushed stress of air travel, the rhythmic clatter of the tracks offered us a rare sense of mindfulness, fostering deep, heartfelt conversations with my companions and fellow backpackers. That journey left an indelible mark on me because it completely transformed my perspective on public transit, proving that the commute itself can be just as enriching and soul-stirring as the ultimate destination.

p1.q: How do you usually commute to work or school?
p1.a: I usually ride my electric scooter to the office every morning. It takes around twenty minutes, which is far quicker than taking the bus because I can effortlessly weave through the city's notorious morning rush-hour traffic.

p1.q: Have your travel habits changed over the past few years?
p1.a: Yes, substantially. I used to rely almost exclusively on ride-hailing motorbikes, but since the new elevated metro line opened near my apartment, I now use the train for most long-distance cross-town trips to avoid seasonal downpours.

p1.q: Do you think public transport in your hometown is efficient?
p1.a: It has definitely improved, but I wouldn't call it completely efficient yet. While modern urban railway lines run punctually, traditional buses frequently fall behind schedule due to severe bottlenecking on narrow thoroughfares during peak hours.

p3.q: What measures can city planners take to encourage more citizens to use public transit?
p3.a: In my view, municipal authorities must prioritise convenience and reliability above all else. Subsidising fares is helpful, but people primarily switch when services are punctual and well-connected. For instance, creating dedicated bus rapid transit corridors prevents vehicles from getting stuck in traffic jams. If public transit becomes demonstrably faster than private driving, commuters will naturally leave their cars at home, resulting in a cleaner urban environment.

p3.q: Do you believe that high-speed rail networks will eventually replace domestic flights?
p3.a: To a great extent, yes, particularly for mid-range intercity journeys. Bullet trains offer massive advantages in passenger convenience because stations are usually situated in city centres, eliminating lengthy airport transfers and security checks. While aviation remains indispensable for crossing vast oceans or continents, high-speed rail is vastly more energy-efficient and comfortable. Consequently, as infrastructure expands, domestic flights along popular regional corridors will likely become obsolete.

travel.sample: I would like to talk about an unforgettable trip I took to Ha Giang, a mountainous province in northern Vietnam, roughly two years ago. I went there with three of my closest university friends, and we decided to do a motorbike road trip to truly immerse ourselves in the rugged landscapes. During our four-day journey, we navigated the winding passes of Ma Pi Leng, which offered breathtaking views of towering limestone peaks and deep valleys. We also took a scenic boat ride along the emerald Nho Que River and stayed at a traditional homestay in a Hmong village. There, we shared home-cooked meals with the host family and learned about their customs, which was an incredible cultural immersion. What made this trip so memorable was the genuine sense of adventure. Conquering steep mountain roads pushed us out of our comfort zones, while the majestic natural scenery made all our exhaustion vanish. Overcoming occasional bike breakdowns together also strengthened our bond, leaving me with treasured memories that I will never forget.

p1.q: Do you like travelling?
p1.a: Definitely, I'm a passionate traveler. Exploring new destinations allows me to escape the daily grind and broaden my horizons. Whenever I get a few days off, I immediately book a trip to recharge my batteries.

p1.q: Where did you go on your last trip?
p1.a: My last getaway was to Da Nang, a coastal city in central Vietnam, about three months ago. I spent most of my time lounging on My Khe Beach and savoring delicious local dishes like Quang noodles.

p1.q: Do you prefer travelling alone or with friends?
p1.a: I certainly lean towards traveling with companions. Sharing unique experiences and splitting travel costs makes the journey far more enjoyable and budget-friendly. Road trips with friends always generate hilarious memories that solo trips simply cannot offer.

p3.q: Does tourism bring more benefits or problems to a country?
p3.a: In my view, tourism brings substantial economic benefits by generating employment opportunities and driving regional development. However, poorly managed mass tourism often leads to severe environmental degradation and overcrowding in heritage sites. While these drawbacks are genuine concerns, sustainable tourism policies and strict regulations can effectively mitigate them. On balance, the economic prosperity and cross-cultural understanding generated by tourism far outweigh its potential disadvantages.

p3.q: Will people travel more or less in the future?
p3.a: I believe people will travel considerably more in the coming decades. Technological advancements in aviation and high-speed rail will make long-distance transit faster and much more economical. In addition, the surge in remote working enables professionals to lead nomadic lifestyles without sacrificing careers. While economic downturns might cause temporary slowdowns, the innate human thirst for adventure ensures a steady rise in global mobility.

volunteering.sample: I would like to talk about a volunteer project I joined last summer, which involved teaching basic English to underprivileged children in a remote mountainous village in northern Vietnam. It took place over two weeks in Ha Giang province, organized by an independent youth charity. I teamed up with around ten university peers who shared a common passion for community development. Our daily routine included planning interactive language lessons, teaching conversational phrases, and organizing outdoor games to boost the children's confidence. We also helped distribute donated stationery and storybooks to set up a modest community reading room. The main reason I decided to sign up was that I wanted to give back to the community and put my academic skills to meaningful use during the holiday. Witnessing the children's genuine smiles and enthusiasm despite their harsh living conditions deeply moved me. It was an eye-opening journey that helped me appreciate my own privileges while making a tangible, positive difference in those young learners' lives.

p1.q: Have you ever done any voluntary work?
p1.a: Yes, definitely. During my second year at university, I participated in a blood donation drive on campus. It was a rewarding experience because I knew my small contribution could potentially save someone's life in an emergency.

p1.q: Would you like to volunteer in the future?
p1.a: Certainly, I would love to join environmental cleanup campaigns in my city. With plastic pollution worsening, spending my weekends picking up litter alongside fellow volunteers would be a very practical way to make an impact.

p1.q: What kinds of volunteer activities are popular among young people in your country?
p1.a: In Vietnam, youth often take part in Green Summer campaigns, teaching children in rural areas or renovating local schools. Tree planting and charity fund-raising for disaster-hit regions are also extremely common.

p3.q: Should voluntary work be compulsory for high school students before graduation?
p3.a: In my opinion, community service should not be mandatory. While it instills social responsibility and builds empathy, forcing teenagers can make it feel like an academic chore rather than an act of kindness. Instead, schools ought to offer incentives like leadership awards or course credits. That way, students participate with genuine altruistic motives rather than simply ticking a graduation box.

p3.q: How can non-profit organizations encourage more people to participate in community service?
p3.a: Non-profit groups can leverage social media to showcase the tangible outcomes of their projects, which inspires trust and engagement. Collaborating with universities or corporate sponsors to offer flexible, micro-volunteering tasks also helps busy individuals get involved. By lowering participation barriers and celebrating volunteers' efforts publicly, organizations can foster a much stronger culture of giving back across different demographics.

weather.sample:
I'd like to talk about an incident last summer when unpredictable weather completely ruined my camping trip. A group of close friends and I had planned a weekend getaway to a picturesque lakeside campsite on the outskirts of Hanoi. We had packed barbecue supplies and tents, expecting clear, sunny skies based on the weekly forecast.

However, right as we arrived and started pitching our tents, the sky turned ominous and pitch-black. Within minutes, a torrential downpour accompanied by fierce gusts of wind broke out. The rain was so relentless that our campsite quickly turned into a muddy swamp, making outdoor cooking entirely impossible.

Left with no other choice, we packed up our soaked gear and took refuge in a small roadside diner nearby. Instead of grilling by the lake, we ended up having steaming bowls of local noodles while listening to the storm rattle the roof.

Initially, I felt terribly disappointed and frustrated because we had spent weeks organizing the outing. Yet, looking back, laughing over our misfortune in that cozy diner actually brought us closer together, making it a surprisingly memorable mishap.

p1.q: What is the weather usually like where you live?
p1.a: I live in northern Vietnam, where we experience a humid subtropical climate. Summers are typically sweltering and rainy, whereas winters can be surprisingly chilly and overcast. Right now, for instance, it is quite muggy and overcast.

p1.q: What is your favourite season?
p1.a: Autumn is definitely my favorite time of the year. The weather is crisp, breezy, and far less humid than summer. I love going for evening walks around the city without sweating profusely, especially in late October.

p1.q: Does the weather affect your mood?
p1.a: Absolutely, it has a direct impact on how I feel. Gloomy, overcast days make me feel lethargic and unmotivated, whereas clear blue skies and bright sunshine instantly give me a burst of positive energy and productivity.

p3.q: Is climate change a serious problem for your country?
p3.a: Yes, without a doubt. Vietnam is one of the most vulnerable nations to global warming. Rising sea levels and prolonged droughts are severely threatening agricultural heartlands like the Mekong Delta. Moreover, extreme weather events, such as unseasonal typhoons and flash floods, have become far more frequent and destructive in recent years. If substantial mitigation strategies aren't implemented soon, the socioeconomic consequences will be catastrophic.

p3.q: How does weather affect the way people live in cities?
p3.a: Weather fundamentally dictates daily urban routines and infrastructure. During severe heatwaves or heavy monsoons, city dwellers tend to retreat indoors, heavily relying on air-conditioned malls and private transport, which often exacerbates traffic congestion. In contrast, pleasant weather fosters active street life and outdoor dining. Ultimately, harsh weather conditions force urban planners and citizens alike to continually adapt their commuting habits and lifestyle to stay resilient.

mistakesVi: Lạm dụng thành ngữ lỗi thời 'rain cats and dogs' – Người bản xứ hiện đại hầu như không dùng cụm này trong văn nói tự nhiên; thay vào đó nên dùng các cách diễn đạt Band 7+ như 'pouring with rain', 'torrential rain' hoặc 'heavy downpour'.

Nhầm lẫn giữa danh từ và tính từ chỉ thời tiết – Rất nhiều thí sinh quen miệng nói 'It was very rain' hoặc 'The weather is very sun' thay vì dùng dạng tính từ đúng là 'rainy'/'sunny', hoặc diễn đạt dạng động từ 'It was raining heavily'.

Phát âm sai trọng âm và nguyên âm của các từ chủ đề quen thuộc – Tiêu biểu là từ 'climate' (/ˈklaɪ.mət/ thường bị đọc sai thành /klaɪ-mết/) hay 'comfortable' (/ˈkʌm.fət.ə.bəl/ bị phát âm thừa âm tiết thành /com-fót-tây-bồ/).

If I had the opportunity to try any career for a while, I’d jump at the chance to become a travel documentary filmmaker. This role involves journeying to off-the-beaten-track locations to capture cultural stories, indigenous traditions, and wildlife on film.

To thrive in this field, one needs a unique blend of technical expertise and interpersonal flair. Besides mastering camera gear, video editing software, and drone piloting, having strong storytelling and adaptability skills is crucial, especially when facing harsh environments or language barriers.

What draws me to this profession is the sheer freedom and sense of purpose. Rather than being stuck behind a desk from nine to five, I would get to immerse myself in diverse communities, documenting disappearing customs before they fade away. The prospect of blending artistic creativity with authentic exploration is immensely appealing.

To prepare for such a drastic leap, I have started taking digital cinematography courses on weekends and upgrading my camera setup. I also plan to produce short travel vlogs across Vietnam to hone my storytelling craft and build a portfolio before pitching to travel networks.

p3.q: Is it better to have one job for life or to change jobs often?
p3.a: Personally, I believe switching jobs periodically brings greater benefits nowadays. While staying with one employer guarantees stability and a predictable pension, changing roles exposes workers to varied corporate cultures, allowing them to diversify their skill sets rapidly. In today's volatile economic climate, versatility and an extensive network are far more valuable than loyalty to a single company. Therefore, occasional career shifts foster stronger professional resilience.

p3.q: Do you think working from home will become more common?
p3.a: Without a doubt, remote work will likely become the standard model across knowledge-based sectors. Advanced cloud tools and collaboration platforms have proven that staff can remain exceptionally productive without enduring grueling daily commutes. Although in-person cooperation remains vital for hands-on industries, most forward-looking firms are already implementing hybrid schedules to cut office overheads and attract global talent, making this trend irreversible.
